does: Adds cream to a hot sauce over low heat and keeps it at a gentle bubble, so that the sauce turns smooth, pale and rich without splitting or boiling hard.

intro.what: Cream is stirred into a sauce at the end over low heat.
intro.why: Cream softens an acid or sharp sauce and gives it body, as long as the heat is kept gentle.

how: Turn the heat down before the cream goes in.
Pour in the cream and stir until the sauce is one even colour.
Let it bubble gently until it coats a spoon. Do not let it boil hard.

cues.text: The sauce is one smooth, even colour and coats the back of a spoon.
Small lazy bubbles, never a rolling boil.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring cream into a fiercely boiling, acid sauce, so that it splits into grainy flecks.
mistakes.fix: Lower the heat first and keep it at a gentle bubble.

mistakes.mistake: Using thin cream, which splits easily in a hot sauce.
mistakes.fix: Use double cream or another cream with plenty of fat.

quiz.question: What does cream do to a sauce?
choices: Makes it smooth and rich, and softens sharp tastes.
quiz.because: The fat in cream softens and enriches the sauce.

quiz.question: What do you do before adding the cream?
choices: Turn the heat up to high.
Take all liquid out of the pan.
quiz.because: A gentle heat keeps the cream from splitting.

quiz.question: How should the sauce look once the cream is in?
choices: Smooth and of one colour, coating a spoon.
quiz.because: A smooth, even sauce shows the cream has blended in.

quiz.question: The sauce turned grainy after the cream went in. What would you change next time?
choices: Add the cream over lower heat and use a richer cream.
Add the cream earlier and boil it longer.
quiz.because: Fierce heat and thin cream are what make it split.
